page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v6 is an ARM-based server instance powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 2835 GB of bundled local disk capacity and supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory subsystem capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core tests, Passmark memory scores, and Passmark database operations. Large-block memory bandwidth read and write operations also rank in the top 10% tier. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the average category. Multi-threaded decompression and static web serving throughput are strong, placing in the top 25%.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a compute-heavy design with relatively low memory capacity per core, which may limit memory-intensive applications. However, the high-capacity local storage and top-tier database benchmark results make it highly cost-efficient for database operations, software compilation, and web serving workloads that require high disk throughput and memory bandwidth without massive RAM footprints. It is also suitable for medium-scale LLM text generation, though it exhibits weaker performance on small-model text generation and large-model prompt processing.
